defects: The page is composed of massive, empty pastel color blocks that create a disjointed, washed-out visual structure, failing to anchor content.
The hero section's 'Unown' vertical text stack on the right feels arbitrarily placed and lacks a functional connection to the terminal UI on the left.
There is no visual rhythm; the alternating pastel sections create a chaotic, 'color-splash' effect that destroys the disciplined spacing and calm density required.
The dark, terminal-inspired UI element is placed on a stark, solid beige block, which feels disconnected from the rest of the page's pastel 'confetti' aesthetic.
The scattered glyphs in the second-to-last section look like floating, unanchored elements rather than a cohesive, pattern-based section, breaking the brand's intentional alignment.
improvements: Remove the large, empty pastel color blocks; use a single, cohesive dark or warm paper background.
Establish a strict 8pt or 12pt spacing grid to replace the chaotic, unanchored section heights.
Integrate the pastel colors as subtle, low-opacity accent lines or gradients, not full-screen voids.

critiques.label: The terminal coding agent that remembers.
defects: The 'Read the docs' text link is underweighted against the 'Star on GitHub' button, breaking visual parity for a secondary action.
The right-hand glyph column is vertically misaligned with the primary content stack, creating an awkward whitespace gap on the right.
The 'INSTALL' tab bar uses a harsh, flat background that clashes with the organic 'paper' texture of the surrounding install card.
The micro-copy at the very bottom of the viewport is cut off, suggesting a poor vertical rhythm or lack of bottom padding in this band.
The vertical rhythm between the 'BETA' tag and the main headline is too tight, compressing the visual breathing room.
improvements: Increase vertical padding above the headline to improve the visual hierarchy of the brand tag.
Align the right-hand glyph column's top edge with the start of the 'Open-source' tagline.
Introduce a subtle drop shadow on the code block to better separate it from the background.

critiques.label: Most agents forget. This one has to prove it rem
defects: Inconsistent left alignment: The subhead 'Three steps...' and the main heading are not perfectly vertically aligned, creating a slight visual break in the leading edge.
Type pairing friction: The pixelated display font and the clean sans-serif body font feel disjointed; the body font looks like a standard default that clashes with the hand-drawn brand.
Visual noise in code block: The monospace text in the file panel uses a generic system font that lacks the terminal aesthetic expected in a developer tool, breaking immersion.
Passive tab labels: The subtext under the tab labels (e.g., 'YOU CHAT', 'IT MINES') is too faint and small, reducing the clarity of the workflow steps.
improvements: Align the subhead flush-left with the main heading for a strong visual anchor.
Increase tab sub-label contrast to 4.5:1 to meet WCAG AA for legibility.
Add subtle hand-drawn underlines to section subheaders to reinforce brand identity.

critiques.label: Every capability, catalogued and filmed.
defects: Left sidebar search input box (No. 001 Websearch) has inconsistent corner rounding compared to the square buttons above it, breaking the pixel-art geometric language.
The 'FILMED' status labels in the left list are right-aligned with varying text lengths, creating ragged visual edges that distract from the list's vertical rhythm.
The terminal window inside the film player lacks clear visual separation from the 'Websreach' header above it; the brown border feels heavy and clutters the bottom half of the card.
The typography hierarchy between 'No 001 · The Crawler Form' and 'Websearch' is too subtle; the secondary label barely registers, making the primary title compete for attention.
Vertical spacing between the 'ALL 23' tab group and the 'SEARCH THE DEX' section is tighter than the gap between individual list items, disrupting the 4/8pt spacing rhythm.
improvements: Align 'FILMED' labels to a consistent right-margin to create a clean, stable vertical edge.
Increase whitespace between 'All 23' tabs and the search area to match internal list rhythm.
Refine terminal window borders with subtle contrast to better separate it from the film header.
Boost visual weight difference between 'No 001' and 'Websearch' for clearer hierarchy.
Standardize corner radii across all UI components to match the pixel-art aesthetic.

critiques.label: What the running engine looks like.
defects: Caption text beneath the main and secondary window mockups is too small and low-contrast, risking legibility on low-end displays.
The right-aligned text 'INSTALL IT AND RUN UNOWN DASHBOARD →' under the surface cards feels floating and disconnected from the main content column.
Vertical alignment of the two secondary window mockups at the bottom is slightly uneven relative to the primary mockup's vertical axis, creating subtle visual noise.
improvements: Increase caption text size by 1px and raise contrast to 4.5:1 for body copy.

critiques.label: The agent built these. They run.
defects: The board card titles are set in a pixel/scanline typeface that is hard to read at 14px, competing with the section headline and undermining WCAG legibility
The tag chips (backend, tech-debt, qa, etc.) are tiny, low-contrast gray-on-dark, failing contrast requirements and looking like afterthoughts rather than a system
The kanban board feels like a pasted-in SaaS widget that betrays the hand-drawn paper/ink brand: zero organic texture, harsh 1px borders, generic dark gray palette
The tab bar (Sigi Bazaar, Cadence, Parley) is cramped and the active tab’s cream pill has no clear relationship to the ink/gold accent system, looking like a stock UI control

The section heading and subhead “Six apps, live. Pick one.” float over the warm paper but the board below is a cold, desaturated dark—no visual bridge (inset shadow, ruled line, or warm border treatment) to anchor them together
improvements: Replace board card titles with a clean 13-14px sans-serif; keep pixel type only for section headings
Increase chip contrast to 4.5:1 and add 1px accent-color borders on tags
Warm the board background with subtle paper grain or a soft ink-toned border to bridge to page

critiques.label: Built & Improved With Unown
defects: Visual hierarchy is inverted: the 2x2 code dashboard grid (right) dominates the 'Loop's Receipts' text column (left), contradicting the narrative flow where text (receipts) should lead and dashboards (proof) support.

Massive, unexplained whitespace in the right two dashboard cards: 'Mission Control — Skills' and 'Memory' cards are approximately 80% empty below their title bars, creating a broken, unfinished look that violates calm density.

Typography lacks discipline: the section headers ('THE MISSION'S ROUNDS', 'THE LOOP'S RECEIPTS') use a small, tracked-out, lowercase-style sans-serif that fights the dominant pixel-art display font, creating a jarring, unintegrated visual rhythm.

Alignment is structurally poor: the left text column and right grid column are not visually balanced. The text column's varying card heights do not align with the right grid's rigid two-row structure, causing the eye to bounce erratically between the two zones.

Color/contrast issue: The 'UNOWN DASHBOARD' header bar in the mockups uses a muddy brown that clashes with the warm gold of the site brand, and the white text on it suffers from borderline legibility compared to the crisp black ink used elsewhere.
improvements: Redesign layout: Stack text receipts full-width top; place dashboard proof grid full-width bottom.
Align empty right-cards with bottom text-card bottom; trim right-cards height to eliminate voids.
Standardize header typography: Drop small tracked sans; use medium-scale pixel font for sub-headers.

critiques.label: Receipts, not promises.
defects: The section 'eyebrow' label 'PROOF' is misaligned with the H1 baseline and lacks vertical rhythm, creating a disjointed visual entry point.
The tab interface relies on subtle background fills that provide insufficient color contrast to clearly distinguish the active vs. inactive states on the paper texture.
The left 'Benchmark' column has inconsistent left-alignment of the metadata text versus the header icons, causing a visual 'ragged' edge on the interior content.
The horizontal progress bars in the right column lack internal spacing between the bar track and the percentage label, making the data hard to parse at a glance.
The 'GET STARTED' button uses a dark fill with a white stroke that breaks the warm paper/ink aesthetic and reduces button contrast on the light background.
improvements: Align 'PROOF' to left edge, increase top margin, reduce font size for better hierarchy.
Increase contrast on active tabs with bold text and a distinct gold or ink underline.
Left-align all metadata text and add a consistent 16px left padding gutter for columns.
Add 8px right padding to progress bars and align percentage labels to the column's right edge.

critiques.label: The name is a pun you have to read twice.
defects: The floating 'C' glyph and scattered asterisk symbols create visual noise that competes with the primary heading, breaking the focal hierarchy.
The 7-column letter grid introduces chaotic color variance (blue/red/green/brown borders) that creates a busy, uncontrolled pattern, ruining the calm density.
The 'FIELD NOTES' footer text is extremely small, creating a WCAG contrast failure and rendering it illegible against the light paper background.
The right-hand sidebar panel feels disconnected; it competes for attention with the main text without a clear visual link or consistent spacing rhythm.
The 'U' letter tile in the grid has a heavy, dark background that breaks the pattern of the other tiles, making it look like an error rather than a selection state.
improvements: Reduce grid borders to a single subtle, monochromatic hairline to restore visual calm and rhythm.
Increase footer text size to 14px minimum to ensure WCAG-legible contrast and readability.
Remove the floating decorative 'C' and asterisk glyphs to reduce visual noise and focus the eye.

critiques.label: The skeptic's questions.
defects: Insufficient tap target for FAQ questions; the text appears small and tightly cropped within the accordion boxes, making them feel more like rows than buttons.
Weak visual separation between the 'FAQ' and 'CHANGELOG' sections; the shift from paper background to light blue is abrupt and lacks a deliberate transition or rule, causing a disjointed feel.
The left-column text block (FAQ header and subheader) is vertically centered against the accordion list, creating negative space that feels unbalanced rather than intentional padding.
The changelog subheader text ('365 entries...') has low contrast against the light blue background, bordering on illegible for users with low vision or glare.
The 'FAQ' and 'CHANGELOG' labels are visually identical in weight to the body text, failing to leverage the pixelated display typeface to establish stronger categorical separation.
improvements: Increase accordion row height by 50% to establish a comfortable, thumb-friendly touch target for the FAQ questions.
Introduce a subtle horizontal rule or distinct section break to clearly delineate the FAQ from the Changelog content.
Left-align the FAQ header to the top of the section to create a stronger, more structured visual anchor.

critiques.label: What has been added, and when.
defects: Severe visual clutter and alignment breakage caused by the fourth card being cut off, creating a jagged, unfinished edge that destroys the grid's rhythm.
The right-hand navigation arrows float in isolated, unanchored whitespace with poor visual proximity to the carousel, failing to establish a clear affordance connection to the cards.
Lack of optical alignment in the card headers: the 'LATEST' tag in the first card disrupts the vertical rhythm and misaligns with the clean headers of subsequent cards.
Confusing density contrast between the light, airy section background and the heavy, boxy card borders, causing the components to feel disjointed rather than integrated.
Inconsistent visual weight of the top header line, which appears like a separate, heavy underline disconnected from the card below it rather than a defining border.
improvements: Crop or mask the overflow cleanly instead of a jagged, cut-off fourth card.
Group navigation arrows with the carousel for better visual proximity and clear affordance.
Standardize card header alignment by removing or integrating the 'LATEST' tag rhythmically.

critiques.label: One afternoon, and then it starts remembering.
defects: Header 'BETA' tag is visually cramped against the 'UNOWN' wordmark, creating a slight collision that disrupts the clean rhythm of the branding block.
The 'SPELL IT IN UNOWN' card header aligns flush to the top edge with insufficient vertical padding compared to the bottom, making the internal layout feel top-heavy and cramped.
The footer section lacks a distinct color or background treatment, causing it to feel visually disconnected from the hero and lacking the clear boundary expected in a polished dark-first design.
The small print disclaimer text in the footer is extremely dense and has low contrast against the cream background, failing to provide a comfortable reading experience for small text.
improvements: Increase left padding for header 'BETA' tag to establish a more generous breathing room from the logo.
Add equal top and bottom padding to the green card's header to balance the visual weight and create breathing room.

defects: Massive empty vertical whitespace below the hero creates a disconnected, broken layout feeling.
The 'UNOWN' vertical text feature creates a fragmented visual flow and poor readability.
Terminal-style card section feels cramped compared to the surrounding excessive white space.
Inconsistent rhythm between the stacked text blocks and the isolated diagram elements.
Nav bar elements appear small and lack clear visual prominence against the light background.
improvements: Collapse redundant vertical whitespace to improve content density and flow.
Reposition UNOWN glyphs horizontally or integrate them as a cohesive visual accent.
Increase spacing consistency between terminal card elements and surrounding sections.

critiques.label: The terminal coding agent that remembers.
defects: High-contrast 'GET STARTED' button in deep magenta clashes with the established warm ink/paper palette, disrupting brand cohesion.
The 'Read the docs' link next to the primary GitHub button suffers from weak visual weight and low contrast, undermining CTA hierarchy.
The header includes a cluttered 'DEMO' tab that feels tacked on and breaks the clean navigation rhythm of the top bar.
The body copy's dark blue-grey text on the cream background creates a slightly muddy, low-legibility experience compared to pure ink.
The 'Unown is in beta' disclaimer text is set in a monospace font that is too small and tightly tracked, reducing scannability.
improvements: Replace magenta button with deep ink or gold to align with warm brand palette and improve visual harmony.
Increase contrast of secondary text and links by switching to pure black ink for body and high-weight labels.
Remove or visually integrate the 'DEMO' tab to establish a cleaner, more confident header hierarchy.

critiques.label: Most agents forget. This one has to prove it rem
defects: Tab rows use inconsistent icon alignment: the 'Work' tab glyph is vertically centered, but 'Learn' and 'Dream' icons sit slightly high relative to the text baseline.
The code block terminal font lacks sufficient line-height and contrast against the beige background, making the outcome text difficult to scan rapidly.
The 'BETA' badge and hamburger icon in the header use uneven horizontal padding, breaking the consistent spacing rhythm established by the logo text.
improvements: Increase terminal text contrast to meet WCAG AA standards for legibility on beige backgrounds.
Standardize tab icon vertical alignment to match the text baseline across all three states.
Unify header padding values to establish a consistent horizontal spacing rhythm across the top bar.

critiques.label: Every capability, catalogued and filmed.
defects: The primary heading 'Every capability, catalogued and filmed.' suffers from severely broken line-wrapping, creating ragged, uneven word spacing that undermines perceived precision.
Filter tabs ('ALL 23', 'SESSION 5') are inconsistent in color, contrast, and spacing; 'ENGINE 6' and 'WORKFLOWS 9' are visually detached, failing to form a cohesive grid.
The table rows ('Websearch', 'Mcp') lack visual separation between the index, name, and status, making scanning difficult; 'FILMED' text is low-contrast and floats ambiguously.
The 'SEARCH THE DEX' header feels ad-hoc and cramped against the input field, with no clear vertical rhythm separating the utility bar from the main data table.
Overall, the warm 'paper' background fails to provide sufficient contrast against the muted green and maroon elements, reducing WCAG readability and the 'dark-first' brand promise.
improvements: Normalize heading word-spacing and constrain line-length to fix broken wrapping.
Unify filter tab styling and establish a strict two-column grid rhythm.
Increase vertical padding between table rows and improve status label contrast.

critiques.label: What the running engine looks like.
defects: Excessive vertical whitespace between the main headline and the first dashboard card creates a disconnected visual gap.
The 'Memory' and 'Session' dashboard previews are nearly illegible; the text is too small and low-contrast against the dark background.
Truncation of the third dashboard title ('SESSION + /DASHBO...') looks like a bug rather than an intentional design choice.
The caption text below the first dashboard ('Overview: KPI band...') is very small and light, failing accessibility contrast ratios.
The top navigation bar feels cramped and disconnected from the 'MISSION CONTROL' label, which sits awkwardly between the nav and the hero text.
improvements: Increase dashboard preview text size and contrast significantly for legibility.
Tighten vertical spacing to create a cohesive, unified visual flow between sections.
Fix dashboard title truncation and improve caption text contrast for accessibility.

critiques.label: The agent built these. They run.
defects: The 'Sigil Focus' tab visually bleeds out of its container and overlaps the 'Sigil Bazaar' text, breaking the UI metaphor.
The dark mode application screenshot is crushed by excessive empty vertical dead space at the bottom.
The 'LIVE DEMO' eyebrow text is an oversized system font that fights the hand-drawn pixel hero typography.
The 'TAP TO TRY IT LIVE' bottom bar lacks internal vertical breathing room, pushing the text to the absolute edge.
improvements: Fix the overlapping tab layout to contain elements within the dark UI frame.
Crop the bottom empty dead space from the application mockup.
Scale down the 'LIVE DEMO' eyebrow to match the pixel display type.

critiques.label: Built & Improved With Unown
defects: Mobile header controls (hamburger and view-toggle) are too close to the right edge with no safe-area padding, risking thumb mis-taps.
The gold accent text on the light paper background has borderline WCAG contrast; the 'verified' and 'promoted' terms wash out against the cream.
The monospace 'hand-drawn' display font is used at a large size but its pixelated stroke weight flickers slightly on mobile LCD, reducing perceived precision.
The four receipt cards are visually identical in border style and spacing, creating a flat list with no visual grouping or hierarchy among the different data types.
The '50 dreams consolidated' card's secondary text is too small and tightly kerned for comfortable reading on a mobile viewport, straining legibility.
improvements: Increase safe-area padding on header controls to 24px.
Increase gold contrast to 4.5:1 ratio for mobile legibility.
Group receipt cards into two visual clusters with varied border weights.

critiques.label: Receipts, not promises.
defects: The 'PROOF' label at the top left is significantly lighter in color and smaller scale than the main 'Receipts, not promises' header, creating a fractured visual hierarchy.
The three data cards at the bottom ('47%', '89.1%', '-16%') have inconsistent bottom padding and lack a distinct container border, causing them to visually bleed into the dark background below.
In the list rows (Benchmarks, Integrity, Models), the hand-drawn icons are vertically misaligned with the secondary text (e.g., 'SIX TRACKS, MEASURED'), creating a jagged left margin.
The '47%' card label 'post-cutoff problems, kimi-k2.5' lacks visual distinction from the title 'LiveCodeBench v6 pass@1', reducing readability of the sub-header.
The transition from the light pink section to the darker bottom section is a hard, unsoftened edge that creates a visual 'cliff' and breaks the 'warm paper' aesthetic.
improvements: Increase 'PROOF' contrast weight to match header prominence, or replace with a more subtle typographic treatment.
Unify padding and add a subtle ink line border to all three data cards at the bottom.
Align hand-drawn icons vertically with primary text, creating a consistent, calm left-margin grid.

critiques.label: The name is a pun you have to read twice.
defects: The 'UNOWN' wordmark in the header utilizes a low-contrast, muted maroon against a light olive background, failing WCAG AA standards for legibility.
A rogue circular control icon is horizontally misaligned, floating inconsistently in the paragraph text and breaking the established left-to-right text flow rhythm.
The 'BETA' badge features a harsh, solid black outline that feels visually too heavy and disconnected from the otherwise soft, hand-drawn sketch aesthetic of the header.
Column alignment in the 4x4 glyph grid is erratic; the border weights between columns appear uneven, and the sub-labels are not perfectly centered under their corresponding glyphs.
The typography scale in the primary body copy is too large relative to the viewport width, forcing an excessively narrow text column that significantly disrupts the reading flow.
An arbitrary, heavy black border separates the top navigation from the section label, which feels visually jarring and disrupts the continuous paper-like background texture.
improvements: Increase 'UNOWN' logo contrast to dark ink, ensuring clear WCAG AA compliance against the background.
Remove or intentionally integrate the rogue circular icon to restore consistent visual flow and alignment.
Standardize grid column borders and perfectly center all sub-labels beneath the corresponding glyphs.

critiques.label: The skeptic's questions.
defects: The 'BETA' badge in the header has insufficient border contrast against the background, making it look like a rendering artifact.
The 'FAQ' small label lacks a clear visual connection to the main heading below, floating in isolation.
The small triangle icons on the left of each accordion item have low contrast and appear detached from the text baseline.
The bottom blue footer band is a hard, unexplained cut with no transition or context, breaking the immersive theme.
The main heading 'The skeptic's questions.' is set in a decorative font that reduces legibility at mobile scales compared to the body text.
improvements: Increase 'BETA' badge border thickness and use high-contrast ink color for legibility.
Group the 'FAQ' label directly under the main heading or style it as a consistent kicker.
Align triangle icons with text baselines and increase their size/contrast for clear affordance.

critiques.label: What has been added, and when.
defects: Floating prev/next arrows at ~340px decouple from the timeline; they float in whitespace with no clear container or affordance anchor.
The second card on the right is clipped at the viewport edge with no visual cue (edge fade, scroll shadow) that it's a scroll target, reads as a layout bug.

Two separate legend lines (caption + bottom) duplicate the interaction description; bottom 'Newest left; cut releas... Scroll or ◀▶ .' collides with the bottom of the card row and creates vertical clutter.
Top-right control cluster (hamburger + monitor) sits on a different tint band than the nav baseline, producing an unintended horizontal color seam.
'4 additions · 5 fixes · 3 alter agent behavior' wraps unevenly under a full-width rule; metrics and rule don't align on a shared baseline grid.
improvements: Tighten vertical rhythm: card spacing from timeline to 48px, legend from card to 24px.
Merge duplicate legend into one 12px caption directly under the scrollable row, left-aligned.
Add right-edge scroll fade (24px gradient) and shadow to signal off-screen card.
Snap arrows into a 36px pill group, baseline-aligned with timeline start/end dots.
Unify top-band background to single tint; remove hard edge between nav and content.

critiques.label: One afternoon, and then it starts remembering.
defects: The CTA button block ('GET STARTED' and 'STAR ON GITHUB') feels vertically isolated from the supporting paragraph above it, breaking the visual flow of the primary message.
The 'SPELL IT IN UNOWN' section is overly dense at the bottom, with the '7/9' counter and terminal input line cramped against the large Unown glyphs, reducing breathing room.

The contrast between the light mint background and the dark green text is strong, but the white text on the dark green buttons/panels feels slightly flat and lacks a subtle drop shadow or bevel to match the 'Game-Boy-inspired' tactile aesthetic.

The alignment of the 'Read the docs' text next to the 'STAR ON GITHUB' button is vertically centered against the button's mid-line, which feels slightly off compared to being baseline-aligned with the button's text.
improvements: Tighten vertical spacing between paragraph and buttons to group them into a single visual unit.
